jobs.description:

Commensurate with experience

**Appointment Type**

Full-time Tenure Track

  

**General Description**

The Department of Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Computer Science at the University of Montevallo (UM) invites applications for a full-time tenure-track Assistant Professor of Chemistry, beginning Fall 2027. Responsibilities include teaching a wide variety of undergraduate chemistry courses for both majors and non-majors including support courses for other majors, academic advising, and service to the University and profession. Preference will be given to applicants with specialization in analytical chemistry or biochemistry. The successful candidate must have evidence of potential for scholarship and excellence in teaching.

  

**Essential Job Duties**

**Overview of the Department of Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Computer Science (****BCMC****)**: BCMC supports undergraduate degree programs in Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Computer Science as well as graduate support courses for the Master of Education in Secondary Education. The Chemistry Program offers Bachelor of Science degrees in Chemistry, including an ACS-certified Chemistry program and a Biochemistry concentration. The average class size in BCMC is approximately 19 students, underscoring our commitment to individualized learning. Smaller class sizes, relative to larger universities, allow faculty to be more engaged with students in the classroom and in advising their academic careers. Instructors may teach up to 15 credit hours per semester.

  

**Additional Duties**

  

**Education and Experience**

A Ph.D. in Chemistry from an accredited institution is required. However, ABD doctoral candidates nearing completion will also be considered. Strong communication skills; a substantive commitment to excellence in teaching undergraduate chemistry courses with students from a wide array of academic and career backgrounds, **as well as the ability and willingness to teach online graduate courses as needed.** Demonstrated ability or potential to engage in scholarly and research activities consistent with departmental standards and the expectations of the University.

  

**Preferred Education and Experience**

None

**Open Until Filled**

**Additional Information**

  

**Additional Statement**

The University of Montevallo does not discriminate against job applicants based on their national origin or citizenship or immigration status. Because of the costs associated with visa sponsorship/transfer, the University typically will not sponsor applicants for a work visa or transfer of an existing visa. No commitment for visa assistance and/or sponsorship can be made until a thorough search is conducted, including a proper and methodical review of all applicants.

  

**EEO Statement**

UM is an Equal Opportunity Institution.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor
jobs.description:
**General Description of the Position**
---------------------------------------

Division of Physics, Engineering, Mathematics, and Computer Science (PEMaCS) - Mathematical Sciences at Delaware State University seeks applicants for a full-time, tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level Qualified applicants must have a Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics/Data Science/Machine Learning/Electrical Engineering or related fields with preference to Data Science and Machine Learning. The Mathematical Sciences Program offers undergraduate degrees in Mathematics, Mathematics with Data Analysis, and Mathematics Education; master’s degrees in applied mathematics; and PhD in Interdisciplinary Applied Mathematics and Mathematical Physics. Delaware State University (DSU), a historically black university with a diverse faculty and student body, has a student population of approximately 5,000 undergraduate and graduate students. DSU is located in Dover, Delaware.

**Essential Functions & Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**
------------------------------------------------------------------

The following are the functions essential to performing this job:
  
1. Teach (on campus) graduate and undergraduate data science courses, as well mathematics courses.
  
2. Actively apply for external funding for research and educational activities.
  
3. Advise graduate and undergraduate students
  
4. Maintain an active research agenda that engages students.
  
5. Serve the Department, College, and University on Committees and in other roles

**Qualification Standards**
---------------------------

1. Education: Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering, or related fields.
  
2. Evidence of the ability to effectively teach students of varying abilities.
  
3. Evidence of the ability to effectively conduct research and write grants.
  
4. Experience with student diversity.

**Performance Standards & EEO Statement**
-----------------------------------------

The criteria for evaluation in this position include, but are not limited to, the following:
  
1. Demonstrate knowledge of the DSU Fundamentals.
  
2. DSU-AAUP CBA requirements.
  
3. Demonstrated excellence in the areas of teaching and research.

EEO Statement

**Delaware State University is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The University does not discriminate on the basis of gender, race, religion, age, national origin, color, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship or disability, veteran or military status, gender identity or genetic information. Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities. The University is committed to the policy of equal employment opportunity in recruitment, hiring, career advancement, and all other employment practices.**

**Description**
Children's Hospital of Philadelphia and the Division of Hematology in the Department of Pediatrics at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seek candidates for an Assistant Professor position in the tenure track. Applicants must have an M.D and/or Ph.D or equivalent degree.
  
  
Teaching responsibilities may include the education and mentoring of graduate students and postdoctoral fellows.
  
  
Clinical responsibilities may include inpatient and outpatient services according to interest for MDs or MD/PhDs.
  
  
Research or scholarship responsibilities may include independent research pursuing fundamental or translational research directly relevant to benign hematology, hematopoiesis, stem cell biology, hemostasis and thrombosis, red blood cell disorders including hemoglobinopathies, bone marrow failure syndromes, or other hematologic diseases. The successful candidate will be expected to secure independent research grant support, usually from federal organizations, in addition to support from participation in collaborative grants.
  
  
As a CHOP-based Penn faculty member, the candidate will have access to exceptional institutional resources, including state-of-the-art core facilities, robust computational and genomic infrastructure, extensive opportunities for collaboration across CHOP and Penn, and unique access to clinical investigators, patient cohorts, and biospecimen resources. A recruitment package, dedicated laboratory space, and outstanding mentorship opportunities will be provided.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Anglophone Poetry Studies
jobs.description:
**Job no:** 541828  
**Work type:** Tenure-Track Faculty  
**Location:** Main Campus (Gainesville, FL)  
**Categories:** Humanities  
**Department:**16200000 - LS-ENGLISH

**Classification Title:**

Assistant Professor in Anglophone Poetry Studies

  

**Minimum Requirements:**

PhD, and record of research/publication and teaching experience in any field or period of American, British, and/or global Anglophone poetry.

  

**Job Description:**

The Department of English at the University of Florida invites applications for a full-time, nine-month, tenure-track Assistant Professor position to teach in the B.A. and Ph.D. programs in the field of Anglophone Poetry Studies, beginning August 16, 2027. We seek candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our community. The successful candidate will be expected to 1) maintain an active writing and publication career, 2) teach four courses per academic year at the undergraduate and graduate level, and mentor and advise undergraduate and graduate students, 3) contribute service to the Department, the University, and the profession.

The Department offers innovative courses and programs at all levels and enjoys productive relationships with other units housed within and beyond the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, including the Center for the Humanities and the Public Sphere.

UF is a major comprehensive, land-grant, research-intensive university, ranked in recent years as among the nation’s top public universities. Gainesville is a city of approximately 150,000 residents in Alachua County. It sits 50 miles from the Gulf of Mexico, 67 miles from the Atlantic Ocean, and within a 2-hour drive to Orlando, Tampa, and Jacksonville. Its many nearby parks, springs, and recreational areas offer year-round outdoor activities such as hiking, biking, diving, and nature photography. Learn more at Visit Gainesville

  

**Expected Salary:**

The salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience, and the compensation includes a full benefits package.

UF offers a strong benefits package for eligible faculty appointments, including health insurance, paid leave (as applicable), and retirement options. Learn more here.

  

**Required Qualifications:**

PhD, and record of research/publication and teaching experience in any field or period of American, British, and/or global Anglophone poetry.

  

**Preferred:**

We are especially interested in candidates with expertise across periods, genres, and national literature. Our ideal candidate would also have demonstrated interest in critical and theoretical approaches to literature and culture. This is not a creative writing position, but courses in Anglophone poetry studies are likely to attract MFA students as well as undergraduates taking poetry workshops.

  

**Special Instructions to Applicants:**

For full consideration, applications must be submitted online. Click on at the top of this posting.

For full consideration, applications must include: (1) a letter of application summarizing the applicant's qualifications, interests, and suitability for the position, (2) a complete *curriculum vitae*, including a list of three references, (3) a statement of teaching goals and practice.

Application review will begin on December 1, 2026, and the position will remain open until filled. Applications received after this date may be considered at the discretion of the search committee and/or hiring authority.

After initial review, writing samples will be requested from selected applicants, as well as letters of recommendation from the listed references. We anticipate Zoom interviews in December or January and campus visits for finalists in the spring term.

All candidates for employment are subject to a pre-employment screening which includes a review of criminal records, reference checks, and verification of education.

The selected candidate will be required to provide an official transcript to the hiring department upon hire. A transcript will not be considered “official” if a designation of “Issued to Student” is visible. Degrees earned from an educational institution outside of the United States require evaluation by a professional credentialing service provider approved by the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES), which can be found at http://www.naces.org/.

  

**Health Assessment Required:**

No

**Advertised:** 23 Oct 2026 Eastern Daylight Time  
**Applications close:** Open until filled

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Mathematics and Statistics
jobs.description:
Job Description

**Job Summary:**
----------------

The Department of Mathematics and Statistics at the University of Nebraska at Kearney (UNK) is accepting applications for a tenure track position starting in August 2027. The Department is looking for a passionate educator with a strong commitment to student success and high-quality teaching. Teaching responsibilities will primarily include face-to-face courses for mathematics majors and non-majors, ranging from college algebra and elementary statistics to upper-level courses. The position also includes expectations for research and publication appropriate to the mission of the University in a related field, as well as service to the department, college, university, and discipline.

  

The position carries a standard teaching load of 12 credit hours per semester, with the possibility of a 3-credit-hour research release each semester. Teaching is the primary responsibility of the position, with research and service also expected in accordance with departmental, college, and university guidelines for continued appointment, promotion, and tenure.

Must be willing to teach in-person and be on campus.

**Required Qualifications:**
----------------------------

* Doctoral degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Mathematics Education, or a closely related discipline earned by the date of appointment.
* Commitment to high-quality, student-centered teaching and student success.
* Potential for scholarly activity and publication appropriate to the mission of the University, including an interest in engaging undergraduate students in research.
* Ability to communicate effectively with students, colleagues, and other university constituents.

**Preferred Qualifications:**
-----------------------------

* Evidence of excellence in undergraduate teaching, including the use of effective, innovative, active, or research-based teaching and learning strategies.
* Experience engaging undergraduates in research or in applying mathematics/statistics in industry or other professional settings.
* Evidence of service and professional engagement at the department, college, university, or community level.

**Additional Information:**
---------------------------

A complete application must include (1) a cover letter detailing your qualifications and how your background fits this position, (2) a curriculum vitae, (3) a 1-3 page statement on teaching that addresses your focus on student success, (4) a 1-3 page research statement outlining past achievements and future goals, including your plans to involve undergraduate students in research, and (5) contact information for three references, at least one who can address your teaching

**About Us:**
-------------

The University of Nebraska at Kearney (UNK) is a public university committed to excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement. As part of the University of Nebraska system, UNK offers a supportive, student-focused environment with the resources of a larger institution. Located in central Nebraska, UNK serves around 6,000 students and is known for its strong academics, welcoming campus culture, and dedication to student success. UNK is looking for individuals who embrace the teacher-scholar mindset and can add to the supportive nature of the campus and department.
  
  
As a University of Nebraska employee, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, retirement, and wellness programs—plus 13 paid holidays each year, generous leave options, and tuition remission.
